name: Prompt Registry Classification Refiner
sprintRole: Iteratively review the full Prompt Kit classification model, prototype bounded taxonomy improvements, turn discovered invariants into executable hooks, and converge the validated classification system to main without renaming canonical prompt identities merely to fit the taxonomy
useWhen: Prompt Kit classes, types, profiles, categories, colors, keywords, filters, or discovery behavior have drifted, overlap confusingly, classify similar prompts inconsistently, or need a deliberate registry-wide classification pass that improves the taxonomy and its enforcement rather than hand-editing a few labels.
inspectFirst: Current default-branch Prompt Kit registries and generated site; classification fields and their actual consumers; filter/search/discovery behavior; prompt IDs/titles as stable identity; adjacent alias/synonym or intent-routing mechanisms so presentation aliases and discovery synonyms are not mistaken for taxonomy; existing classification tests, builders, validators, hooks, CI, and recent overlapping prompt/filter work.
expectedOutput: A measured classification baseline, explicit field semantics and ownership, one or more bounded prototype migrations, executable hooks or validators for every newly proven invariant that can be checked deterministically, focused regression coverage, generated-site parity, preserved canonical prompt identities, and the exact validated classification result integrated into current main.
nextStep: Classify the current registry baseline, choose the smallest high-value ambiguity as prototype 1, implement that classification slice plus its enforceable hook, rebuild and falsify it through the real Prompt Kit filters/search, then continue from the new evidence until no bounded classification defect remains and merge the exact green head to main.
proofGate: Every classification field has a non-overlapping documented role grounded in current consumers; canonical prompt IDs and useful titles survive reclassification; aliases, human display titles, keywords, and intent/discovery synonyms are not silently promoted into canonical taxonomy; each iteration is an executable prototype with before/after evidence; every deterministic invariant discovered during the sprint is enforced by the nearest practical validator/hook before the next migration slice; generated registry/site parity and focused classification behavior pass on the exact head; and the validated result is contained in refreshed main.
copyContent:
REFINE THE PROMPT KIT CLASSIFICATION SYSTEM ITERATIVELY. REVIEW THE WHOLE REGISTRY, IMPLEMENT HOOKS AS CLASSIFICATION RULES BECOME PROVABLE, AND CONVERGE THE EXACT VALIDATED RESULT TO MAIN. DO NOT RENAME PROMPTS MERELY TO MAKE THE TAXONOMY LOOK CLEAN.

Repo: `EndeavorEverlasting/web-excel-repair-triage` or resolve the current Prompt Kit repository from context
Classification pain, if known: xyz_classification_gap_or_infer_from_evidence

MISSION
Treat Prompt Kit classification as an engineered information architecture, not a one-time relabeling exercise. Inspect the full effective registry and the UI/discovery surfaces that consume it; make the smallest useful classification improvement; run it as a real prototype; falsify the result; convert each proven classification invariant into an executable hook or validator as you go; then repeat until the bounded classification system reaches a fixed point and the exact green result is integrated into current main.

1. REFRESH AND BASELINE THE ACTUAL CLASSIFICATION SYSTEM
Start from refreshed default-branch truth. Inspect the combined registry, generated Prompt Kit, builder, filter/search/discovery consumers, registry helper, focused tests, hooks/CI, and overlapping prompt/filter branches or PRs. Inventory the fields that currently participate in identity, classification, presentation, and discovery. Do not infer semantics from field names alone.

Build a compact baseline that answers for every relevant field: what it means today, who writes it, who consumes it, allowed/current values, collisions/near-duplicates, empty or overloaded buckets, and whether it is identity, taxonomy, presentation, or discovery metadata. Measure practical defects such as ambiguous labels, inconsistent sibling prompts, filter branches that mean different things in different places, singletons that should be merged, overloaded classes that need a useful split, or discovery keywords doing work that belongs in taxonomy.

2. KEEP IDENTITY, TAXONOMY, PRESENTATION, AND DISCOVERY DISTINCT
Preserve canonical prompt IDs and useful prompt names unless a separate explicit rename requirement exists. Classification work must not manufacture new prompt identities merely because a different label sounds better.

Determine the repository-specific meaning of fields such as `type`, `class`, `profile`, `category`, `color`, and `keywords` from current code and contracts before changing them. In particular:
- stable ID/name are identity, not a classification migration target by default;
- human aliases/display titles are presentation identity, not canonical taxonomy;
- keywords, triggers, and intent synonyms primarily serve discovery/routing unless the repository explicitly assigns them another role;
- color is visual semantics unless current consumers prove it is a classification axis;
- profile/registry placement is ownership or behavior only to the extent current builders/tests actually use it.
Do not collapse these systems into one universal label.

3. ITERATE AS PROTOTYPES, NOT AS A BIG-BANG TAXONOMY REWRITE
Use this loop:
`BASELINE -> HYPOTHESIS -> SMALLEST PROTOTYPE -> REBUILD -> USE/FALSIFY -> HOOK -> MIGRATE NEXT SLICE -> REFRESH -> CONTINUE`.

Prototype 1 should attack the highest-value bounded ambiguity, not attempt to rename the whole registry. Exercise the prototype through the real Prompt Kit UI/filter/search/discovery path or the closest executable consumer. Compare before/after behavior and inspect surprising prompts at both sides of the boundary. A prototype is evidence; it is not automatically the final taxonomy.

After each pass, ask what the result taught you about the classification model. Keep the successful invariant, repair the failed hypothesis, or revert the slice if evidence says the old boundary was better. Continue with the next smallest migration only after the prior classification rule is understandable and protected.

4. IMPLEMENT HOOKS AS YOU LEARN THE RULES
Whenever an iteration establishes a deterministic invariant, enforce it immediately in the nearest existing owner rather than leaving the rule as prose. Reuse current validation/harness patterns. Examples include registry validation, focused semantic assertions, allowed-value checks, uniqueness or normalization checks, classification-consumer parity, generated-site checks, pre-commit/pre-push hooks, or CI path triggers.

Do not add a hook for subjective judgment that cannot be checked reliably. Do not create one giant universal classifier merely to centralize everything. Prefer small checks at the boundary that owns the invariant. A later prototype may strengthen an earlier hook when new evidence reveals an edge case.

5. CLASSIFY BY BEHAVIOR AND CLOSURE, NOT TITLE ALONE
When deciding where a prompt belongs, compare trigger, mission, owned scope, expected output, proof gate, and closure condition. Similar wording does not imply the same class; different wording does not imply different classes. Use representative sibling prompts and boundary cases to test each proposed class.

If the taxonomy needs a new value, prove that existing values cannot express the distinction without making discovery/filtering worse. If two values mean the same thing in practice, migrate toward one canonical value and protect it. Preserve intentional distinctions where downstream behavior or user navigation benefits from them.

6. PROVE DISCOVERY AND FILTER BEHAVIOR
Rebuild the canonical Prompt Kit after each tracked classification migration. Exercise hierarchical filters, search, prompt identifiers, favorites/hotkeys when classification metadata participates, and any registry/profile views affected by the change. Confirm that a user can still find the expected prompts by natural language and canonical ID. Classification cleanup must not silently break search/discovery or turn synonyms into taxonomy.

7. SECOND-PASS FALSIFICATION
After the first apparently green classification state, inspect the registry from the opposite direction: sample prompts from every changed bucket, inspect neighboring unchanged buckets, search for old/new classification labels, run edge-case filter combinations, and review generated output plus focused tests. Turn every concrete in-scope miss into another prototype pass. Do not manufacture churn when the evidence reaches a bounded fixed point.

8. CONVERGE TO MAIN
Refresh the remote default branch immediately before final proof. Reconcile moved base/dependencies without discarding owned work. Run the strongest focused classification tests, registry helper validation, generated-site parity/build checks, filter/search/discovery regressions, applicable hook/CI checks, and `git diff --check`. If the exact validated head is merge-authorized and clean, merge it into current main in the same sprint. After merge, refresh main and prove containment of the integrated SHA rather than requiring head equality if main advanced again.

DELIVER
Report: baseline classification defects; field-semantics map; each prototype hypothesis and result; classification migrations; hooks/validators added or strengthened; prompts intentionally left unchanged and why; generated-site/filter/discovery proof; commit/PR/merge state; resulting main SHA; remaining classification debt or `none` at the bounded fixed point.

FAIL-CLOSED
Do not perform a registry-wide relabeling without an executable prototype and rollback boundary. Do not rename stable IDs/titles as a substitute for classification. Do not confuse aliases or human-facing artifact names with taxonomy. Do not treat search keywords/intent synonyms as canonical class labels merely because they improve discovery. Do not weaken hooks/tests to accept the migration. Do not stop at a green feature branch while safe authorized mainline integration remains.
